q.t: On how many occasions has the UK hosted the Olympic Games, and in which years?
q.e: The UK has hosted the Olympic Games on three occasions: 1908, 1948 and 2012. The main Olympic site for the 2012 Games was in Stratford, East London.

q.t: Where did the British team finish in the medal table at the 2012 Olympic Games?
q.e: The main Olympic site for the 2012 Games was in Stratford, East London. The British team was very successful, across a wide range of Olympic sports, finishing third in the medal table.

q.t: Where did the Paralympic Games have their origin?
q.e: The Paralympics have their origin in the work of Dr Sir Ludwig Guttman, a German refugee, at the Stoke Mandeville hospital in Buckinghamshire. Dr Guttman developed new methods of treatment for people with spinal injuries and encouraged patients to take part in exercise and sport.
o: In the work of Dr Sir Ludwig Guttman at Stoke Mandeville hospital
In the work of Baroness Tanni Grey-Thompson
At the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff

q.t: Which of these statements is correct?
q.e: Sir Roger Bannister was the first man in the world to run a mile in under four minutes, in 1954. Sir Jackie Stewart is a Scottish former racing driver who won the Formula 1 world championship three times.
o: Sir Roger Bannister was the first man to run a mile in under four minutes
Sir Jackie Stewart was the first man to run a mile in under four minutes

q.t: Who captained the English football team that won the World Cup in 1966?
q.e: Bobby Moore (1941-93) captained the English football team that won the World Cup in 1966. England's only international tournament victory was at the World Cup of 1966, hosted in the UK.

q.t: In which year did Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean win Olympic gold medals for ice dancing?
q.e: Jayne Torvill (1957-) and Christopher Dean (1958-) won gold medals for ice dancing at the Olympic Games in 1984 and in four consecutive world championships.

q.t: For what achievement is Sir Steve Redgrave known?
q.e: Sir Steve Redgrave (1962-) won gold medals in rowing in five consecutive Olympic Games and is one of Britain's greatest Olympians.
o: Winning rowing gold medals in five consecutive Olympic Games
Winning six Olympic gold medals in cycling
Winning the Formula 1 world championship three times

q.t: Which TWO of these people won the London Marathon six times, according to the handbook?
q.e: Baroness Tanni Grey-Thompson won 16 Paralympic medals, including 11 gold medals, and won the London Marathon six times. David Weir is a Paralympian who has won six gold medals over two Paralympic Games and has also won the London Marathon six times.

q.t: What did Dame Ellen MacArthur achieve in 2004?
q.e: Dame Ellen MacArthur (1976-) is a yachtswoman and in 2004 became the fastest person to sail around the world singlehanded.
o: She became the fastest person to sail around the world singlehanded
She won two Olympic gold medals for running
She became the first Briton to win the Tour de France
She won Olympic gold in the heptathlon

q.t: In 2012 Bradley Wiggins became the first Briton to win which event?
q.e: Bradley Wiggins (1980-) is a cyclist. In 2012, he became the first Briton to win the Tour de France. He has won seven Olympic medals.

q.t: Which TWO distances did Mo Farah win gold medals for at the 2012 Olympics?
q.e: Mo Farah (1983-) is a British distance runner, born in Somalia. He won gold medals in the 2012 Olympics for the 5,000 and 10,000 metres and is the first Briton to win the Olympic gold medal in the 10,000 metres.

q.t: How many track and field events make up the heptathlon, which Jessica Ennis won in 2012?
q.e: Jessica Ennis (1986-) is an athlete. She won the 2012 Olympic gold medal in the heptathlon, which includes seven different track and field events.

q.t: Which of these statements is correct?
q.e: Andy Murray (1987-) is a Scottish tennis player who in 2012 won the men's singles in the US Open. He is the first British man to win a singles title in a Grand Slam tournament since 1936.
o: Andy Murray was the first British man to win a Grand Slam singles title since 1936
Andy Murray was the first British man to win a Grand Slam singles title since 1966

q.t: What is the most famous cricket competition, and between which countries is it played?
q.e: The most famous competition is the Ashes, which is a series of Test matches played between England and Australia.
o: The Ashes, between England and Australia
The Ashes, between England and India
The Six Nations, between England and Australia
The Super League, between England and Australia

q.t: Which of these is NOT one of the six countries in the Six Nations Championship?
q.e: The most famous rugby union competition is the Six Nations Championship between England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, France and Italy. The Super League is the most well-known rugby league competition.

q.t: Which TWO horse-racing events are named in the handbook alongside Royal Ascot?
q.e: Famous horse-racing events include Royal Ascot, a five-day race meeting in Berkshire attended by members of the Royal Family; the Grand National at Aintree near Liverpool; and the Scottish Grand National at Ayr.
o: The Scottish Grand National at Ayr

q.t: To which century can the modern game of golf be traced back, and to which country?
q.e: The modern game of golf can be traced back to 15th century Scotland. It is a popular sport played socially as well as professionally. St Andrews in Scotland is known as the home of golf.

q.t: What is distinctive about The Open Championship in golf?
q.e: The Open Championship is the only 'Major' tournament held outside the United States. It is hosted by a different golf course every year.
o: It is the only 'Major' tournament held outside the United States
It is the oldest tournament in the world
It is the only Major played on grass
It is always held at St Andrews

q.t: Where and when was the first tennis club founded?
q.e: Modern tennis evolved in England in the late 19th century. The first tennis club was founded in Leamington Spa in 1872.

q.t:
Is the statement below TRUE or FALSE?
The Wimbledon Championships is the oldest tennis tournament in the world and the only Grand Slam event played on grass.
q.e: The most famous tournament hosted in Britain is The Wimbledon Championships, which takes place each year at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club. It is the oldest tennis tournament in the world and the only 'Grand Slam' event played on grass.

q.t: Which of these statements is correct?
q.e: A British sailor, Sir Francis Chichester, was the first person to sail single-handed around the world, in 1966/67. Two years later, Sir Robin Knox-Johnston became the first person to do this without stopping.
o: Sir Robin Knox-Johnston was the first to sail around the world single-handed without stopping
Sir Francis Chichester was the first to sail around the world single-handed without stopping

q.t: In which year did motor-car racing start in the UK?
q.e: There is a long history of motor sport in the UK, for both cars and motor cycles. Motor-car racing in the UK started in 1902. The UK continues to be a world leader in the development and manufacture of motor-sport technology.

q.t: How many ski centres are there in Scotland, according to the handbook?
q.e: Skiing is increasingly popular in the UK. Many people go abroad to ski and there are also dry ski slopes throughout the UK. There are five ski centres in Scotland, as well as Europe's longest dry ski slope near Edinburgh.

q.t: Which TWO stadiums are named in the handbook as major venues for sporting events?
q.e: Many sporting events take place at major stadiums such as Wembley Stadium in London and the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.
o: The Scottish Exhibition and Conference Centre
